atlas-ru.0001: Graduate recruiting is visible in spring: MISIS’s job fair on 30 March 2026 brought together about 60 employers and 5,200 students, and Yandex announced its 2025 internship season in February with a candidate event on 20 March; its internships run three to six months and can be combined with study.
atlas-ru.0002: The job boards, university career pages and employer internship pages read (hh.ru, HSE, MISIS, Yandex, Sber) are in Russian and state no English requirement; no page read describes English-language hiring for graduates.
atlas-ru.0003: We found no current graduate employment or unemployment rate for Russia; the most reliable statement read is HeadHunter’s ranking of 411 universities by employer demand for their graduates, built on more than 500,000 graduate CVs from 2021–2022 (published April 2023), which put HSE University first.
atlas-ru.0004: The UK advises against all travel to Russia and the US says do not travel, both citing the war against Ukraine and the risk of detention. The EU has adopted 21 sanctions packages, the latest in July 2026, binding on everyone under EU jurisdiction. Visa and Mastercard cards issued abroad do not work there. This guide does not rate demand in Russia; the rankings and figures below describe the cities’ size, not a recommendation.
atlas-ru.0006: No family is rated: this guide does not assess graduate demand in Russia, and the one economic figure read for Moscow’s role dates from before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
atlas-ru.0007: Russia was not covered by the research library before this record.
atlas-ru.0008: Italy’s Viaggiare Sicuri advice and the Council of the EU’s sanctions page could not be read; the EU position is taken from the European Commission’s page.
atlas-ru.0009: Study visas, work rules, entry for EU passports and whether particular jobs would breach sanctions were not researched: check the sanctions rules with a qualified adviser before accepting any offer.
atlas-ru.0010: Rosstat’s and Mosstat’s own pages were not read: Moscow’s population is a mayoral statement reported by a business weekly, its output is the city’s own estimate as reported by a rating agency, and St Petersburg’s figures are Petrostat’s as quoted in a policy briefing, so the two cities’ figures are not from one compiler. No pay or rent figure is used: the Moscow (2025) and St Petersburg (11 months of 2025) averages found cover different periods.
atlas-ru.0011: Country brief: travel advice and sanctions first, then Moscow and St Petersburg as a statistical picture

atlas-ru.0020: The Moscow city government’s analytical centre said in April 2021 that the Moscow metropolitan area accounted for more than a quarter of Russia’s GDP and almost half of its stock of foreign direct investment.
atlas-ru.0021: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Russia because of its continuing invasion of Ukraine; it reports an increased risk of British nationals being detained, Russia’s record of holding foreign nationals as leverage, a high likelihood of terrorist attacks, and drone attacks disrupting airports.
atlas-ru.0022: The US State Department rates Russia Level 4, do not travel, citing the war with Ukraine, the risk of wrongful detention, arbitrary enforcement of laws and terrorism, and tells US citizens in Russia to leave immediately.
atlas-ru.0023: St Petersburg is Russia’s second-largest city; its gross regional product in 2023 was RUB 10,908 billion, about EUR 117.5 billion at the official average exchange rate.
atlas-ru.0024: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Moscow 100th and St Petersburg 104th of 117 financial centres (103rd and 110th in March 2026), the only Russian centres listed.
atlas-ru.0025: The Fortune Global 500 of 2026 lists Sberbank (rank 64), Rosneft (109) and Lukoil (239) as headquartered in Moscow and Gazprom (89) in St Petersburg; Fortune gives them 291,795, 302,100, 88,950 and 501,000 employees. Fortune’s pages say nothing about sanctions: read the sanctions claim before any dealings with Russian companies.
atlas-ru.0026: The mayor of Moscow told President Putin that the city had 13.3 million residents on 1 January 2025, after natural growth of 4,800 in 2024.
atlas-ru.0027: The rating agency Expert RA, citing the Moscow city government’s own estimate, reports Moscow’s gross regional product in 2023 at RUB 31.8 trillion, 4.0% more than in 2022 in comparable prices, and says the city accounts for about 20% of the GRP of all Russian regions.
atlas-ru.0028: St Petersburg had 5.563 million residents on 1 January 2025 according to Petrostat, the regional statistics service; a Centrum Balticum policy briefing notes that Gazprom has moved its head office to the city from Moscow, and that foreign-trade statistics for the port stopped being published after April 2022.
atlas-ru.0029: Large Russian employers such as Yandex and Sber recruit students through paid internships of three to six months, and the job site HeadHunter ranks universities by how much employers want their graduates, with HSE University first. The UK and US advise against travel to Russia and EU sanctions bind EU persons, so for most readers of this guide this describes the Russian market rather than a route to take.
atlas-ru.0030: Paid internships at large IT and finance employers
atlas-ru.0031: No survey ranks the routes in Russia; this is first because the large employers found recruit this way. Yandex planned 2,800 interns in 2025, 20% more than the year before, paid under the Labor Code for three to six months, and says 54% of its 2024 interns moved to full-time posts.
atlas-ru.0032: Sber’s internship through its School 21 lasts three to six months on a temporary employment contract and pays 73,700 RUB a month at full employment in Moscow; it is a chance to receive an offer of permanent work.
atlas-ru.0034: hh.ru is the largest Russian job board and has a section for young specialists; SuperJob’s Start of Career section promotes practice and internships with leading employers.
atlas-ru.0035: University career centres and job fairs
atlas-ru.0036: MISIS’s spring job fair on 30 March 2026 brought together 5,200 students and about 60 employers, with express interviews and job invitations.
atlas-ru.0037: HSE University’s Career Development Centre lists vacancies and internships, offers over 500 consultations a year and reports over 150 partner companies; its project career schools in 2026 were run with Avito, PSB and Yandex Cloud.
atlas-ru.0038: We found no survey of how much introductions count in Russian graduate hiring; this is our reading that they matter at smaller firms.
atlas-ru.0039: Spring is the visible season: MISIS’s fair was on 30 March 2026, and Yandex announced its 2025 internship season on 12 February 2025 with an event for candidates on 20 March.
atlas-ru.0040: Internships of three to six months fit the student calendar; Yandex lets interns combine the placement with study. We did not establish opening dates for Sber’s intakes.
atlas-ru.0041: HeadHunter’s ranking of 411 universities by graduate demand, built from more than 500,000 graduate CVs from 2021–2022 (published April 2023), put HSE University first overall and first among Moscow universities in law, economics and finance, and in HR and psychology.
atlas-ru.0042: HSE’s Career Development Centre and MISIS’s fair both bring employers onto campus; Sber says it values students of its School 21.
atlas-ru.0043: MISIS spring job fair, 30 March 2026: about 60 employers and 5,200 students, with express interviews.
atlas-ru.0044: HSE Career Marathon and project career schools run by the HSE Career Development Centre (Avito, PSB and Yandex Cloud in March to May 2026).
atlas-ru.0045: Yandex candidate event Y&&Y Lab, 20 March 2025, in Moscow.
atlas-ru.0046: HeadHunter’s ranking puts HSE University first among Moscow universities in law, economics and finance, and in HR and psychology, by employer demand for its graduates.
atlas-ru.0047: Sber runs its own paid internships; its School 21 route lists higher demand for Java, QA, DevOps and systems analysis and lower for Go and mobile development. Check that any Russian bank you apply to is not under sanctions.
atlas-ru.0048: Yandex hires interns for frontend, backend, mobile, analytics and machine learning, and since 2025 for marketing and PR, finance, product management, procurement, HR and law; nearly a third of its developers are former interns.
atlas-ru.0049: Avito’s project career school “Case laboratory of analytics” ran with HSE in May 2026; Yandex Cloud held a career school on AI solutions for social tasks with HSE in April 2026.
atlas-ru.0050: The visible peaks are in spring (MISIS on 30 March, Yandex’s event on 20 March) while the internships themselves run for three to six months; there is no single national season.
atlas-ru.0051: The internship pages read target students and recent graduates by level of study, not by degree; we found no page stating that a master’s is expected. This is our reading.
atlas-ru.0052: The library’s visa guide says foreign documents need an apostille and a Russian notarised translation: translations sworn in Italy or elsewhere in Europe have no legal value in Russia. We found no page on degree recognition, as the Rosobrnadzor site could not be opened.
